bayesval

bayesval is an R package for the external validation of survival prediction models: taking a Cox proportional-hazards model developed elsewhere and asking how well it discriminates, calibrates, and supports clinical decisions in a new — often small and event-poor — validation cohort. It keeps the familiar finite-sample validation estimators that clinicians and methodologists already use, but evaluates each one across the posterior survival draws of a Bayesian model, so every performance measure is reported as a posterior distribution with a credible interval instead of a single point estimate. A pre-specified deployment gate then reads off as one posterior probability that the model is fit for local use.

The same propagation works for apparent, internal, and internal-external designs, but external validation — deciding whether a model developed elsewhere can be trusted in a new setting — is the problem the package is built around, and the one every worked example below illustrates.

This covers the full validation toolkit — Harrell/Uno/Gonen-Heller/Antolini concordance, time-dependent AUC, calibration-in-the-large, calibration slope, ICI/E50/E90, D-calibration, IPCW Brier/IBS/IPA, R²_D, and decision-curve net benefit — each reported as a posterior distribution with a credible interval. The core idea: every performance estimator M is treated as a functional M(S, data) of a posterior survival object and the validation data. Evaluate the existing estimator at each posterior draw; the collection of per-draw values is the posterior distribution for that finite-sample estimator.

Two uncertainty sources are kept explicit: model-parameter uncertainty from the posterior survival draws, and evaluation-sample uncertainty from a Bayesian bootstrap over the validation set. No new point estimators are introduced; propagate_metric() is the propagation wrapper.

Status

bayesval is a research package under active development and accompanies the survival-validation manuscript listed below. The fast examples use the coxph backend and run without Stan. Full Bayesian MCMC examples use the stan_pwexp backend and require a working rstan toolchain; they may take several minutes.

Installation

Install the package from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wmotte/bayesval")

The modelling core needs only the imported package dependencies, including survival, dplyr, purrr, tibble, and ggplot2. Optional backends and comparators need additional Suggested packages:

install.packages(c("posterior", "loo", "BART", "riskRegression", "pec",
                   "timeROC", "survC1", "CPE", "dcurves", "ggdist"))

# Optional, platform-sensitive: needed only for the full Bayesian Stan backend.
install.packages("rstan")

Install optional packages only for the backend or metric family you intend to use. Stan setup is the slowest part of the toolchain; the quick start below uses only the survival-based coxph path.

Quick start 

library(bayesval)

set.seed(1); n <- 500
dat <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rbinom(n, 1, 0.4))
dat$time   <- rexp(n, 0.15 * exp(0.8 * dat$x1 - 0.5 * dat$x2))
dat$status <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.7)
hz <- as.numeric(quantile(dat$time[dat$status == 1], c(.25, .5, .75)))

ps <- fit_bayes_survival(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ x1 + x2, dat, hz,
                         backend = "coxph", S = 300)           # survival-only

disc <- propagate_many(ps, list(harrell  = metric_harrell_c,
                                uno      = metric_uno_c,
                                antolini = metric_antolini_c))
posterior_table(disc)                                          # median [95% CrI]

propagate_metric(ps, metric_harrell_c, weights = "bootstrap")  # + eval-set uncertainty
ppc_calibration(ps, horizon = 2)$ppp                            # calibration PPC
posterior_net_benefit(ps)$p_useful                              # decision-curve layer

posterior_table() returns one row per metric with the posterior mean, median, credible interval, draw counts, and a reliability flag. Adding weights = "bootstrap" widens the target from model-parameter uncertainty alone to model plus validation-sample uncertainty. ppc_calibration() returns a posterior predictive p-value for calibration at the requested horizon.

Model backends

Every backend returns the same model-agnostic psurv object: an [S x n x H] posterior survival array plus the linear predictor. Downstream metrics are therefore backend-agnostic.

backend needs use when
coxph survival you want fast examples, teaching code, or a no-Stan fallback
pwexp survival you want a piecewise-exponential Poisson-trick PH model with a Laplace approximation
stan_pwexp rstan you want the primary full-likelihood Bayesian piecewise-exponential PH workflow
bart BART you want a nonparametric Bayesian survival comparator
stan_surv rstanarm with stan_surv aspirational/conditional; not available in the CRAN rstanarm release

MCMC fits are gated by check_mcmc_gate() before any metric is reported. The gate checks split-Rhat, effective sample size, and divergent transitions. prior_sensitivity() refits under several log-hazard-ratio prior scales to check robustness.

Documentation

The pkgdown site is the main reference:

  • package site: https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/
  • function index: https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/
  • local entry point for writing a new metric: ?propagate_metric
  • full package help: help(package = "bayesval")

Posterior metric objects have summary() methods that report the median, credible interval, finite-draw counts, and an unreliability flag when more than 5% of draws are non-finite.

Worked examples live in vignettes/, and most are external validations on public survival cohorts:

  • worked_example.R — Rotterdam → GBSG breast cancer (the headline example)
  • showcase_pbc.R — Mayo PBC, randomized → non-randomized patients
  • temporal_validation.R — one Rotterdam-trained model on a later Rotterdam era against GBSG
  • worked_example_lung.R — NCCTG lung, split by recruiting centre
  • worked_example_colon.R — colon adjuvant trial, split by treatment arm

showcase_small_cohort.R runs the deployment-gate showcase on a small simulated cohort with a known oracle. Heavier Stan articles (worked_example_stan.R, small_sample_stan_vs_laplace.R) are pre-rendered outside the normal pkgdown build; see articles/README.md for that workflow.

Development checks

For a lightweight local check without rebuilding vignettes:

R CMD build --no-build-vignettes --no-manual .
_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_=false R CMD check --no-manual --ignore-vignettes \
  bayesval_0.1.0.tar.gz

_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_=false is useful on machines without the heavier Suggested packages. A complete CRAN-style check should install all Suggested packages first.

Citation and reproducibility

bayesval is the software companion to:

Otte WM, Kampman SL, […] A Bayesian framework for validating survival prediction models: posterior credible intervals for discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. in prep.
